name: LIFX Color / SuperColor A19 1100 lm (Matter, US)

matter.note: LIFX's Matter list includes LHLA19E26US, LCM4 edition only (part A19L4AE26); units whose firmware starts with v3 have no Matter. CSA lists 'LIFX SuperColor A19 (1100 lumens)' under Feit SKUs, not this model number.

apple_home.note: Pairs with Apple Home via Matter on the LCM4 edition. Check the firmware version in the LIFX app: v3 firmware means no Matter.

google_home.note: LIFX lists Google Home on the product page and has a Google Home setup guide; it can also pair via Matter.

alexa.note: LIFX lists Alexa on the product page and has an Alexa setup guide; it can also pair via Matter.

smartthings.note: LIFX's support guide links your LIFX account in the SmartThings app. The LCM4 edition can also pair via Matter with a SmartThings hub.

home_assistant.note: Official LIFX integration controls lights over the local network (LIFX LAN protocol). The Matter integration is an alternative.

hubRequired.note: Here this means needing a bridge or hub for basic app control. It joins 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi directly and is controlled from the LIFX app.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's LIFX integration talks to the bulb on the local network without the LIFX cloud.

colorType.note: Full colour plus white from 1500 to 9000 K.

lumens.note: 1100 lm, sold as a 75 W equivalent; 11.5 W at full brightness.

summary: Four of the five big platforms connect to the LIFX SuperColor A19 1100 lm (US) through LIFX's own integrations: Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings and Home Assistant, with no hub. Apple Home is the exception. It pairs over Matter, and only the LCM4 edition of this bulb (part A19L4AE26) has Matter. The bulb itself is a full-colour E26 at 1100 lumens with whites from 1500 to 9000 K, on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. Home Assistant controls it locally over the LIFX LAN protocol.
caveats: Apple Home needs the LCM4 edition (part A19L4AE26); if the LIFX app shows firmware starting with v3, the bulb has no Matter.
